By Lemma~\ref{core:assembly-general}(ii), the other two tests are planar precisely when $H_b+cw+bw$ and $H_b+cw+bc$, respectively, are planar. Hence both are nonplanar, while $H_b+cw$ is planar, using the path $cp'w$ in $B$.
Every component of $H_b-\{b,c,w\}$ has neighborhood $\{b,c,w\}$ by three-connectivity of $G$.
If there were two, planarity and Lemmas~\ref{core:assembly-general}(ii) and~\ref{lem:flat-replacement} would make both single vertices, making both tests planar. Thus this interior is connected.

The triangle completion of $H_b$ is a minor of $G$, using the internally disjoint paths $bpc$, $bqap'w$, and $cq'w$ for $bc,bw,cw$.
Lemma~\ref{r2:planar-splitting} therefore gives a nonplanar, $K_5$-minor-free graph
\[
(H_b+cw+bc+bw)/cw=(H_b+cw+bc)/cw=(H_b+cw+bw)/cw.
\]
Write $x$ for the contracted vertex. Retain a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision using Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction}, with attachments $b,x$ and added edge $bx$.
The subdivision uses $bx$, since $(H_b+cw)/cw$ is planar.
Separate $x$ back into $c,w$, keeping each retained incident edge at its original end and one interior neighbor at each attachment.
Both tests still have the retained subdivision as a minor after contracting $cw$, and the other two tests still have three bridges adjacent to $X$.
Thus a proper reduction would give a proper nontoroidal minor of $G$.
The enumeration~\supp{E15} lists all reduced subdivisions and all assignments of the edges at $x$ back to $c,w$.
